principles: Compatibility first: legacy full-mode repositories remain valid.
Prompt body authority belongs to the package registry, while project-local files carry only host-specific entrypoints and configuration.
Thin mode must be explicit and verifiable before any default behavior changes.
drivers: Reduce init file footprint and prompt drift noise.
Keep Codex adapter verification evidence hard and gate-consumable.
Avoid absolute symlink portability traps in cloned repositories.

options.name: A: keep full mirror only
cons: Continues drift noise and symlink portability issues

options.name: B: delete project prompt files immediately
C: add registry-backed thin mode with legacy dual path
pros: Creates migration path with testable hashes
cons: Requires more code and dual-mode tests

chosen: C: add registry-backed thin mode with legacy dual path
rationale: This is the only option that moves prompt authority into the package while keeping existing full-mode repos and adapter gates functional. It lets projects opt into thin assets after registry verification exists, instead of deleting files first and repairing breakage later.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy full-mode verify_codex starts failing because registry mode changes shared assumptions.
preMortem.trigger: checkAgentMirror no longer sees expected files or material hash paths change unexpectedly.
preMortem.consequence: Existing Codex adapter stories are blocked in REVIEW/DONE.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep legacy mirror check unchanged unless manifest explicitly selects registry mode; add tests for both modes.

preMortem.scenario: Thin mode passes check but dispatch cannot render prompts in a real worktree.
preMortem.trigger: Prompt registry is not wired into the dispatch or render path used by agents.
preMortem.consequence: Users get lightweight files but lose reviewer/implementer prompt functionality.
preMortem.mitigation: Expose registry renderer and add smoke tests comparing rendered output to existing templates.

preMortem.trigger: Managed asset check treats all prompt paths as stale safe instead of local edits.
preMortem.consequence: User customizations are lost and trust in init/check is damaged.
preMortem.mitigation: Only omit prompt assets from registry-mode requirements; do not add automatic deletion in this milestone except existing safe generated stale handling.

preMortem.scenario: Thin init is confused with production authority or receipt verification.
preMortem.trigger: Manifest or docs imply registry verification is gate authority beyond adapter asset integrity.
preMortem.consequence: Local checks are overclaimed as production DONE evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Document thin assets as adapter/runtime hygiene only; preserve authority receipt wording.
